attack_technique: Command and Control: Application Layer Protocol (Web Protocols)
description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) to avoid detection. Botnets use periodic beaconing to maintain command-and-control channels, often disguising traffic as normal web browsing.

patterns.description: Regular, automated communication patterns that reveal C2 activity.

features.name: Periodic Inter-Arrival Time
features.description: The standard deviation of flow inter-arrival times (Flow IAT Std) is unusually low or shows a repeating pattern, indicating automated, scheduled communication rather than organic human browsing.

features.name: Long Flow Duration with Low Activity
features.description: Flows have abnormally high duration (Flow Duration) with relatively few packets exchanged, characteristic of keep-alive connections to C2 servers waiting for commands.

patterns.description: Characteristics of the data payload exchanged in botnet communications.

features.name: Small Uniform Packet Sizes
features.description: Packets exchanged are consistently small and uniform in size, typical of short command-and-control messages (check-in, heartbeat, status updates) rather than diverse web content downloads.

features.name: Asymmetric Traffic Pattern
features.description: Very few backward packets (Total Bwd Pkts) compared to forward packets, as the infected host sends beacons out but receives minimal commands back during idle periods.

patterns.description: How botnets abuse legitimate protocols and ports.

features.name: Web Port Abuse
features.description: C2 traffic flows over standard web ports (80, 443, 8080) to blend in with legitimate HTTP/HTTPS traffic and bypass firewall rules.

features.name: DNS-based C2 Tunneling
features.description: Some botnets use DNS queries (port 53) as a covert channel for command-and-control, encoding data within DNS request and response fields.

patterns.description: How to distinguish botnet C2 from legitimate periodic traffic.

features.name: Legitimate Background Services Resemblance
features.description: Background update services, telemetry, cloud sync applications, and software update checks can produce similar periodic patterns. Distinguishing requires analyzing destination reputation and payload entropy.
